subject.title: RFC: Readiness Conditions and Standard Hosting Profiles

question: Should v1 accept the complete condition/provider/profile contract, or first land only core condition normalization and the four standard profiles while staging plugin providers and derived operator profiles?
rationale: The branch is technically coherent and well proven, but it defines permanent configuration, plugin API, support-profile, and fail-closed upgrade behavior whose acceptable scope and rollout order require maintainer intent.

options.title: Stage extensibility
options.body: Accept core condition normalization and standard profiles first, preserving compatibility projections while deferring plugin providers and derived operator profiles to a follow-up RFC or phase.

options.title: Accept full v1
options.body: Adopt providers and operator-derived profiles now, explicitly owning the larger plugin and configuration compatibility surface from the first release.

options.title: Keep researching
options.body: Leave the RFC draft and implementation candidates open until maintainers have additional operational evidence or an alternative readiness model.

recommendation.title: Stage extensibility
recommendation.body: Accept core condition normalization and standard profiles first, preserving compatibility projections while deferring plugin providers and derived operator profiles to a follow-up RFC or phase.

likelyOwner.reason: Their adjacent Gateway architecture RFC makes them the strongest available routing candidate for coordinating the cross-area runtime ownership decision.
